-90.10250,29.93750.name: Audubon Fertility
-90.10250,29.93750.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Lindsay Wells, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-0.09693,51.51492.name: CREATE Fertility
-0.09693,51.51492.desc: A clinic mapped in OpenStreetMap as offering fertility treatment. OpenStreetMap holds what somebody chose to map, so a country with few points here may be thinly mapped rather than thinly served. That is the reverse of the national registers alongside it, which are close to complete for one country and silent everywhere else. This layer is a cross-check and a source of leads, not a count.

-0.19926,51.46124.name: Concept Fertility
-0.19926,51.46124.state: 14 Point Pleasant, Wandsworth Park, London, SW18 1GG
-0.19926,51.46124.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

91.14000,29.65000.name: 西藏阜康医院
91.14000,29.65000.state: 西藏自治区（1家） — 西藏自治区拉萨市城关区罗布林卡路18号
91.14000,29.65000.desc: A medical institution approved by China's National Health Commission to perform assisted reproduction. Approved for: ICSI — a single sperm injected into the egg; IVF with embryo transfer; insemination with donor sperm; insemination with the partner's sperm. All of its approvals are in formal operation. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Approval is compulsory in China and performing assisted reproduction without it is unlawful, so this list is a register rather than a directory of members. It names every approved institution in the country, which is more than almost any other state publishes. The address did not geocode, so this point sits at the centre of the province rather than at the institution.

-97.15342,49.89148.name: University of Winnipeg
-97.15342,49.89148.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, December 2025
-97.15342,49.89148.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, December 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-71.09000,42.36390.name: eGenesis
-71.09000,42.36390.desc: Uses editing to remove porcine retroviruses from the pig genome as well as to reduce rejection — the retrovirus problem being the one that stalled xenotransplantation for decades, because a virus crossing with the organ would arrive inside a patient whose immune system had been deliberately suppressed.

8.65400,49.87600.name: Merck KGaA — Life Science
8.65400,49.87600.desc: Supplies reagents, cell-culture media and CRISPR licences to laboratories everywhere, and holds foundational patents on CRISPR use in eukaryotic cells. That puts it on both sides of the editing business at once — selling the materials and licensing the right to use the method — which is a position no other supplier holds.

6.13600,46.22300.name: World Intellectual Property Organization
6.13600,46.22300.desc: Administers the treaties under which patents are filed internationally, including the Patent Cooperation Treaty route used for nearly every biotechnology application. It also hosts the long-running negotiation on genetic resources and traditional knowledge, where the question of whether a patent must disclose where its biological material came from has been open for over twenty years.

26.72000,58.38000.name: Estonian Biobank
26.72000,58.38000.desc: Holds genetic data on roughly a fifth of the adult Estonian population, run by the state, with results returned to participants through the national health system. It is the clearest working example of a national genomic programme operated as public infrastructure rather than as a research asset or a company holding.

-77.02600,38.88870.name: Global Genome Biodiversity Network
-77.02600,38.88870.state: Washington DC — an international network of biorepositories
-77.02600,38.88870.desc: An international network of institutions holding genomic samples representing the diversity of non-human life, and the layer above the national biobanks: the standards body and index rather than a store. Its existence answers a question this map keeps running into — an engineered crop event carries an OECD identifier that follows it across borders, while a wild tissue sample generally carries only whatever the holding institution wrote down. A network that agrees common records for biodiversity samples is doing for wild genetic material what the identifier system did for commercial events, and it is doing it voluntarily rather than under a treaty.
